title: DeepSeek plans 160,000-chip Huawei Ascend cluster in Inner Mongolia
subtitle: The Chinese AI lab intends to run its models on domestic silicon at gigawatt scale — inference only, with Nvidia still doing the training.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: DeepSeek plans to deploy at least 160,000 Huawei Ascend 950DT accelerators at a new data center in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, according to reporting first published by TechNode on September 7. The chips will run inference — user-facing responses from DeepSeek's models — while training will continue on Nvidia hardware. At roughly $16,000 per chip, the buildout implies about $2.56 billion in silicon alone, with the wider site targeting gigawatt-scale power.

The order matters because it would be the largest known cluster of Chinese-made AI accelerators, and the first at frontier scale to be committed to a Huawei part rather than an Nvidia one. DeepSeek's decision to split the workload — Ascend for inference, Nvidia for training — is a working answer to the question every Chinese AI company now faces: how much of the stack can move to domestic silicon without giving up model quality. Inference is the easier half to migrate, and it is where most compute cost eventually lands.

The plan lands into a year of accelerating Chinese chip nationalism. Huawei has been publicly targeting AI-training parity with its Atlas 950 SuperPoD announced at WAIC in July, and China's ministry of commerce added AI-model export restrictions the same month. DeepSeek itself began an in-house inference chip effort earlier this year. A 160,000-chip Ascend deployment gives Huawei the reference customer it needs — and gives Beijing an answer to US export controls that does not depend on smuggled H200s.

For learners: the split between training silicon and inference silicon is the single most important architectural decision inside a modern AI company, and it is where cost, latency, and sovereignty all trade off against each other. Watch what workload runs on which chip — the answer tells you more about a company's economics and its regulatory exposure than any model benchmark.
